Weekly Connection read past its 7-day window (age 56d); 1 signal read(s) past the 35-day window: retail-sales(44d)

signals_in_scope.name: Retail Sales (YoY)
signals_in_scope.existing_summary: Spending is still up 6.88% year-over-year as of May, and it picked up 2.1 points from last month. Not accelerating, but not breaking either. People are spending; they just don't feel great about it.

signals_in_scope.name: Consumer Sentiment (U. Michigan)

source.name: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (via FRED)

signals_in_scope.existing_summary: As of the latest reading, the University of Michigan confidence index sits at 49.8 — the bottom of its three-year range. It's down 6.6% from last month. Households still expect prices to keep climbing, which is part of why confidence keeps sliding.

signals_in_scope.name: AI API / Inference Pricing Trend
signals_in_scope.existing_summary: The price of comparable AI keeps dropping fast across the major labs. Shipping an AI feature costs a lot less than it did a few months ago.

signals_in_scope.name: Frontier AI Model Release Activity
signals_in_scope.existing_summary: Three major new AI models in the last two weeks — the top of the field is moving fast.

weekly_connection_in_scope.title: Two economies, same week
weekly_connection_in_scope.observation: Consumer confidence is at 49.8 — its three-year floor — and people expect prices to keep rising. May inflation re-accelerated: CPI at 4.25% and PPI at 6.42%, both near multi-year highs. Retail spending is still up 6.88% year-over-year, so wallets haven't closed yet. Meanwhile, top AI model prices dropped roughly 60% over six months, and new frontier models are releasing every few weeks.
